Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR NYLON FABRIC FOR MAKING MOUNTAINEERING EQUIPMENT
0. FOREWORD
Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 December 1986, after the draft finalized by the Silk, Man-Made Fibres and Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 Nylon fabrics are nowadays extensively used for tents, windproof jackets, trousers and other mountaineering applications. Such fabrics if designed to meet certain specific requirements such as resistance to low temperature and resistance to high velocity winds, will reduce the requirement of importing clothing, tents and other items even for expeditions to Antarctica, which is a regular feature now. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular this standard is complied with, the final value, observed expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant in the rounded off value should be the same as that value in this standard. requirement of or calculated, rounded off in places retained of the specified

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of four varieties of coated nylon fabric suitable for the manufacture of mountaineering equipment after coating with neoprene, polyurethane or polyvinyl chloride (PVC) resin. .1.2 This
(see 3.3). 2. MANUFACTURE standard does not specify the shade, feel, etc, of the cloth

2.2 Basic Fabric - The basic nylon fabric shah be evenly and uniformly woven, and free from spinning, weaving and other defects likely to affect the appearance or serviceability of finished material UnIeSs otherwise specified, the fabric shall be heat (see also 3.2.8). set. 2.3 CoatingThe basic fabric shall be coated with suitable polyurethane, neoprene or poIyviny1 chIoride resin composition. The coating shall be uniformly applied on one side of the basic fabric. It shall firmly adhere to the fabric and shall be smooth, pliable and free from tackiness, stains, pinholes and other manufacturing defects. The coating shah not have any disagreeable odour. 3. 3.2.1 pH ValueThe pH value of aqueous extract of the finished fabric when tested by the cold methods prescribed in IS : 1390-1983* shall be between 6'0 to 8'0.
3.2.2 Water Soluble Matter - The water soluble matter, of the finished fabric when tested by the method prescribed in IS : 3456-1966t shall not be more than 2'0 percent. 3.2.3 Dimensional Change - The dimensional change of the finished fabric when tested by the method prescribed in IS : 1299-1984: shall not be more than 2'0 percent in either warp or weft direction. 3.2.4 Flexibilip be such that the warp and weft Appendix D. of Coating - The flexibility of the coated fabric shall average overhang is not greater than 10 cm in both directions when tested by the method prescribed in

*Methods for determination of pH value of aqueous extracts of textile materials (first revision ) . tMethod for determination of water soluble matter of textile materials. $Method for determination of dimensional changes on washing of fabrics woven from rayon and synthetic fibres ( second revision ).

`

6

IS :11915 - 1986 3.2.5 Resistance to AgeingThe finished fabric shall be aged at 70f2"C for 168 hours in an air oven as prescribed in Appendix E. The average breaking strength of the aged fabric shall not be less than 90 percent of the average original breaking strength. After the fabric has been aged, there shall be no cracks, softening or signs of brittleness.
3.2.6 Resistance to Low .Temperature - The coated fabric when exposed to a temperature of -50�C for 6 hours shall not show any sign of appreciable stiffness and shall remain flexible. The coating shall not crack when the specimen, while at this temperature, is bent sharply flat back on itself, coated side on outside.
NOTE This temperature may by achieved by using dry ice.

use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the NOTE -The Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which Standard marked is devised and supervised by BE and operated by the producer. products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
